extracted.intended_audience: Principal investigators (PIs) preparing NIH grant resubmissions who received a Summary Statement
extracted.subtask_description: Practical step-by-step guidance for PIs on how to analyze, respond to, and (if necessary) challenge reviewer critiques when preparing an NIH resubmission, including drafting the one-page Introduction and interacting with Program Officers and colleagues.

rubrics_metrics.name: Do not overreact
rubrics_metrics.description: Do not overreact; resist the urge to immediately fire off an emotional email or phone call to NIH personnel or reviewers.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This is the first 'what not to do' — avoid immediate emotional contact with NIH staff or reviewers. Take time to analyze comments rather than responding impulsively.

rubrics_metrics.name: Consult collaborators and key colleagues
rubrics_metrics.description: Consult with collaborators and key colleagues on the project, as well as any other trusted colleague whose experience might be helpful (e.g., someone who has served on a study section or has been very successful at obtaining NIH research funding).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Assemble a group with relevant experience to get diverse perspectives on critiques; include people who have served on study sections if possible.

rubrics_metrics.name: Meet with the group to analyze reviewer points and develop strategy
rubrics_metrics.description: Meet with the group to go through each point in depth, discussing the group's reactions to it and developing a strategy for responding to that point.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Work systematically through reviewers' comments, recording which require changes, which you will rebut, and how you'll present responses in the resubmission.

rubrics_metrics.name: Contact the Program Officer named on the FOA
rubrics_metrics.description: After you and your project team have completed your analysis of the reviewers' comments, contact the Program Officer named on the Funding Opportunity Announcement (FOA).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Program Officers typically attend study section meetings and may know of reviewer comments not in the Summary Statement; a call may solidify or change your thinking and can provide tips that increase likelihood of a successful challenge.

rubrics_metrics.name: Finalize and revise the research plan to address reviewer comments
rubrics_metrics.description: After you've talked to the Program Officer, finalize your ideas for changes to the research plan, including how you plan to address the reviewer comment(s) you disagree with. Revise the research plan to incorporate these changes.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Make concrete revisions to the research plan rather than relying solely on explanations in the Introduction; integrate agreed-upon changes into the application text.

rubrics_metrics.name: Write the Introduction to the resubmission (one-page summary)
rubrics_metrics.description: Write the Introduction to the resubmission. For most NIH grants, this is a single page that summarizes your response to each reviewer comment.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use this one page to concisely map reviewer critiques to your responses and any changes in the grant. Be precise and organized so reviewers can quickly see how concerns were addressed.

rubrics_metrics.name: Resist the urge to ignore comments you disagree with
rubrics_metrics.description: Resist the urge to ignore the comments you disagree with.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Even if you disagree, address the comment explicitly in the Introduction rather than omitting it; omission can be viewed negatively by reviewers.

rubrics_metrics.name: Respond to every major comment
rubrics_metrics.description: It is essential to respond to every major comment.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Make sure all substantive criticisms are acknowledged and responded to; failing to address major points can undermine the resubmission's chances.

rubrics_metrics.name: When disagreeing, present a strong, logical, and persuasive justification
rubrics_metrics.description: If, after careful analysis and discussion, you still disagree with a reviewer's critique, it is essential that you present a strong, logical, and persuasive justification for doing so in the Introduction.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Ground your disagreement in scientific reasoning and evidence rather than rhetoric; make the rationale clear and defensible.

rubrics_metrics.name: Be courteous and nonconfrontational
rubrics_metrics.description: Be courteous and nonconfrontational when presenting responses or disagreements.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Tone matters: polite, professional phrasing reduces defensiveness and increases credibility when explaining why a critique was not adopted.

rubrics_metrics.name: Acknowledge the reviewer's concern
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Start by recognizing the point raised before explaining your response or rationale; this signals you took the critique seriously.

rubrics_metrics.name: Be clear and polite; avoid apology, argument, and emotion
rubrics_metrics.description: Be clear and polite; avoid apology, argument, and emotion.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use neutral, explanatory language rather than apologetic or emotional phrasing. Avoid combative or defensive language that could appear unprofessional.

rubrics_metrics.name: Avoid defending your experience, expertise, credentials, or qualifications
rubrics_metrics.description: Avoid defending your experience, expertise, credentials, or qualifications.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Let scientific reasoning and revisions speak for competence rather than asserting qualifications as a rebuttal to critique.

rubrics_metrics.name: Describe any revision made and cite the scientific reason; indicate if no change
rubrics_metrics.description: Describe any revision you made in response to the comment, citing the scientific reason for your position; if you made no change in your research plan in response to the comment, indicate that.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Explicitly link each reviewer point to either a concrete revision (and where it appears) or a clear scientific rationale for keeping the original approach; be transparent about decisions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Do not use cost or logistics as a reason for not addressing a comment
rubrics_metrics.description: Do not use cost or logistics as a reason for not addressing a comment.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Arguing that a change is too expensive or logistically difficult is not an acceptable justification for ignoring substantive scientific concerns.

rubrics_metrics.name: Have trusted colleagues review the Introduction before submitting
rubrics_metrics.description: Always ask one or two trusted colleagues to review the Introduction before submitting the resubmission application.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Have peers confirm that responses are rational, non-argumentative, and clearly presented; outside readers can catch tone or logic problems you missed.
